gaps.construct: hand-written Future::poll step returning Poll<()> and registering a Waker in Context
gaps.description: Scribe's concurrency is structured and implicit (`together`, `pipeline`, `workflow`); there is no notion of a resumable step, an executor, a task context or a waker, so the whole contract with the runtime is lost and Poll/Context/Waker are opaque stand-ins.

gaps.construct: AtomicUsize state shared between Sender and Receiver with Acquire / AcqRel ordering and compare-and-swap updates
gaps.description: The doc forbids mutable sharing between tasks and has no atomics or memory orderings; the atomic is hidden behind an opaque capability and the ordering is a label word that means nothing to the checker.

gaps.construct: UnsafeCell<MaybeUninit<Waker>> accessed in `unsafe` blocks, guarded by a state bit
gaps.description: The only escape hatch is `trust`, which records a reason and owner but has no scope, so it is unclear which following lines it covers; the invariant linking the bit to the cell's initialisation cannot be written.
No reference-counted shared ownership exists; Inner is modelled as an owned field, which misstates who can see it.
No macros; each use is spelled out as a three-line `choose`.

gaps.construct: RestoreOnPending guard whose Drop restores the coop budget unless made_progress() was called
gaps.description: `hold` releases a resource on every exit but cannot run conditional behaviour on drop; linear `consumed` types would force consumption on the Pending path too, which is the opposite of the intent.

gaps.construct: inner.as_ref().unwrap() (panic on None) and binding the payload for the rest of the function
gaps.description: No panic, and `choose` binds the payload only inside its arm; unwrapping for the remainder of the body needs a var plus repeated matching, or an invented failure.
Turned into a named failure SenderHasNoInner, which adds a `fails with` line the original API does not have.
`trust` is a single line with no block, so the doc does not settle which statements a trust covers.

gaps.construct: calling an operation for its side effect and discarding its result (State::set_tx_task(&inner.state);)
gaps.description: No statement form for a discarded result is shown; written as `let ignored be ...`.

doc_rules_contradicted: Because values are never shared mutably between tasks, there is nothing for a lock to protect, and no way to forget one.
Structured concurrency only. A task cannot outlive its scope
invented_syntax: choice Poll used as a return protocol with an executor
trust used to scope over following statements
notes: Runtime-level async primitives are a deliberate blind spot of the design: the doc offers structured concurrency for users but nothing for implementing the runtime that provides it, so tokio-style code is out of scope unless Scribe gains a foreign or unsafe sub-language. The control flow itself (three early Ready returns, then Pending) translates fine; everything that makes it correct is outside the language.
